result:
Everything is green: `bun run typecheck` clean, `bun test` 7/7 passing, and `bunx guren check` reports 0 failures.

I added a public JSON feed at `GET /api/posts` in a new `routes/api.ts` (registrar `registerApiRoutes`, wired into `routes/web.ts` next to `registerAuthRoutes`), registering the route as `api.posts.index` with its contract declared on the route itself: a `query` schema (`ApiListPostsQuerySchema` in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` — coercing `page` with a default of 1 and an optional `author`, both positive integers, so `?page=0|abc` and `?author=0|abc` are rejected with a 422 JSON body by the router before the controller runs) plus a `resource: { data: [PostResource] }` response hint, exactly like the existing `posts.search` route — so after `bun run codegen` the regenerated `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` and `.guren/routes.gen.ts` carry `api.posts.index` with a typed `response: { data: Array<Data.Post> }`. The handler is `PostController.apiIndex` (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`): it pages through `Post.withPaginate('author', …)` at a fixed 10 per page, newest first (`createdAt desc`, `id desc` as a tiebreak), optionally filtered by `authorId`, and returns `{ data: PostResource[], meta }` where `meta` comes from the core `paginate()` helper (`currentPage`, `lastPage`, `perPage`, `total`, `from`, `to`). Note I used `withPaginate` rather than the `Post.newQuery().with('author').paginate()` chain the Inertia `index` action uses, because the query builder's `paginate()` silently drops eager-loaded relations — the author would have come back missing (the site's `/posts` page has that same gap today; I left it untouched per the "unchanged" requirement). Tests for the feed — pagination, author filtering, the combined case, the empty-author case, and the four invalid-parameter cases — live in `tests/PostController.test.ts`, building their own fixtures after a `resetDatabase()` and restoring the seeded baseline afterwards.
